source_snapshot.test_name_items: SOL session by ipmitool (Check Volatile Bit Rate rate)
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Send command: ipmitool -I lanplus  -U <User> -P <Password> -H <IP address> sol info
Check Volatile Bit Rate should be 115200.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Check Volatile Bit Rate Procedures & Criteria should match below:
    Volatile Bit Rate (kbps)        : 115.2
2. Output should have human readable characters.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- SOL session by ipmitool (Check Volatile Bit Rate rate): open a SOL session via ipmitool and verify the negotiated volatile bit rate (ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" sol info 2>&1) then ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" sol activate 2>&1 | head -n 40; SOL is interactive.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return `ipmitool sol info` (bit-rate parameters) + the first SOL console lines so the user confirms the SOL session + volatile bit rate are correct.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Partial due assumed operator readability check.

original_test_intent: Verify the intended BMC SOL endpoint reports volatile bit rate 115.2 kbps and can produce readable console characters in a bounded session.
original_method: Read SOL parameters, activate the mapped session, capture output and terminate safely.
manual_activity: Engineer approves endpoint/session policy and expected output; the read-only rate check and PTY transcript can run automatically.
required_inputs: Protected credentials, ownership, timeout and recovery
safety_requirements: Do not activate over an owned session.
Protect secrets and verify target identity.
Send no arbitrary input and terminate cleanly.
No automatic retry; retain raw parameter/output evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Run sol info, parse/normalize 115.2 kbps versus 115200 bps, open bounded SOL, check readable output and terminate.
engineer_actions: Approve endpoint/session contract and formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: sol info/activate fit, but `head` is not session control and plaintext credential form is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use documented ipmitool with secret-safe authentication, PTY timeout and explicit SOL escape.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Volatile Bit Rate 115.2 kbps/115200, readable output, script and 10/0 minutes remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Identity preflight, collect full sol info, normalize rate, activate one bounded session, validate output encoding, exit and verify cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform SOL and installed ipmitool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds endpoint identity and deterministic session handling.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Activation can conflict with another console owner.

project_override_considerations: Equivalent textual units may be normalized, but the raw value and mapped endpoint must be preserved.
expected_evidence: Full sol info and rate parsing

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: 115200 bps and 115.2 kbps are equivalent, not contradictory; source is coherent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Missing mapping/credentials are inputs; all core software observations are automatable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps commands but replaces pipeline with safe session lifecycle.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates final engineer verdict from automatable readability evidence.

review_improvement: Binds the rate to the exact SOL endpoint and proves live readable output without leaving a stale session.
independent_technical_reasoning: Both parameter parsing and character-stream validation are deterministic software checks; a human need not watch the terminal once endpoint and expected encoding are approved.
